title: Web: run screens
summary: The run screens handle the hard behavior with care. The workspace loads a snapshot, replays the events after a cursor, then opens the event stream from that cursor and deduplicates by sequence. Writes use server idempotency keys and version guards. Empty states are deliberate, colors come only from semantic tokens, accessible names are in place, and Playwright covers reconnects, duplicates, gaps, a cut stream and refusals. The cost sits in one place. RunWorkspaceView is a single function of 677 lines with complexity 39. It does the data loading (snapshot, event-page replay, a second refresh path driven by a counter, and the result download), runs the EventSource with its reconnect timer, deduplicates through a Map, merges live text, derives view state during render and draws about fifteen regions. 17 commits for 16 stories have edited it. Error handling is the weakest dimension. The workspace treats every failed read as temporary: it keeps polling a denied or missing run every second, and it never leaves 'Loading' on 403, 422, 5xx or a contract error. Three components also report a lost write reply as a failure and send any retry with a new idempotency key, so an owner can record one provider charge twice. Smaller costs recur across the area: status words and tones, money and time formats, the summarizer rule and the command senders are each written more than once; contract unions are widened to string; error and admission replies are cast although generated parsers exist; run-list and run-panel import each other; and pure logic sits in .tsx files that the node:test runner cannot load. The refactor can be done in steps. First move pure lib/runs modules out with unit tests. Then add load and stream hooks with an explicit state machine that keeps snapshots in cursor order. Then split the screens into section components. This is a static review. It is not runtime evidence.

scores.why: Strict TypeScript flags and the project lint pass, and the pages are thin Server Components, but 10 type assertions at trust boundaries, no denied state, a client-only inspector and a fresh idempotency key per press fall short of DH-06.
Pages compose views and views compose children clearly, but run-list and run-panel import each other and other screens import vocabulary, hooks and constants from screen modules.
9 of the 13 files have functions over 60 lines. RunWorkspaceView (677 lines, complexity 39) is the largest function in the app, and 17 commits have edited it.
The small pure helpers are good (withDelta, wallTime, brief), but each main component mixes fetching, state machines, product rules and markup, and multi-step flows are tracked with boolean flags.
Files are where you would expect them, but the 10 run components sit flat among the 43 files in apps/web/components, and there is no lib/runs or feature folder to receive extracted code.

The replay-then-stream design with server idempotency and version guards is sound. It is weakened by an unordered refetch on every event, no request aborts, counters used as effect triggers and client-side fetching for a static inspector.
Comments explain why and cite decisions and stories throughout. A few mechanics, such as blanking the events before parsing a page and draining response bodies, have no stated reason.
Generated parsers validate every successful read, but error replies, the admission reply and the stream's cursor frame are cast, and contract unions are widened to string.
The run page retries forever on 401, 403, 404 and 422 and hangs on contract errors, and lost write replies are reported as failures. ContinueRun shows the right pattern.
Playwright covers reconnect, deduplication, gaps, stream cuts, controls and refusals, but none of the pure stream, merge or rule logic has a unit test.
Well commented and covered by browser tests, but the workspace hotspot, duplicated vocabulary and formatting, and inconsistent error states make every run story costly.

strengths.title: Snapshot, replay, then stream, with cursor-based reconnects and deduplication by sequence
strengths.evidence: apps/web/components/run-workspace.tsx:242-272 loads the snapshot, replays every page after the cursor and only then opens the EventSource from that cursor. Lines 175-181 deduplicate by sequence. Lines 235-239 close the browser's own retry, because it 'would resume from a stale URL'. apps/web/tests/browser/run-workspace.spec.ts:83-151 and 252-265, and stream-result.spec.ts:101-122, exercise dropped connections, duplicates, gaps and a cut result stream in a real browser.

strengths.title: Generated runtime parsers on every successful read
strengths.evidence: Each successful read is parsed: parseRunWorkspace (run-workspace.tsx:194, run-panel.tsx:68), parseRunList (run-list.tsx:193), parseRunInspector (run-inspector.tsx:32), parseToolUseList after the body is typed unknown (tool-uses.tsx:127-133), parseModelList and parseModelPolicyState (run-disclosure.tsx:58-59), and parseRunEvent for each event (run-workspace.tsx:146). They check JSON against the generated schemas (packages/api-client/src/runtime.ts:142-149).

strengths.title: ContinueRun treats an unknown outcome as unknown
strengths.evidence: apps/web/components/continue-run.tsx:20-21 keeps the Idempotency-Key in a ref until the outcome is known, and line 39 reuses it. Lines 47-51 treat a lost reply or any 5xx as 'may have started'. Lines 68-69 reset the key only after a refusal that followed no unknown attempt. This is the pattern WRUN-03 asks the other writers to adopt.

strengths.title: A reusable, abortable hook for paginated reads
strengths.evidence: useToolUses (apps/web/components/tool-uses.tsx:102-147) aborts a superseded read with an AbortController and says why (line 111), loops over cursor pages, and is reused by the workflow monitor (apps/web/components/workflow-monitor.tsx:7).

strengths.title: Deliberate empty, loading and failure states
strengths.evidence: RunList separates loading, unavailable, an empty workspace (with a link to Home) and no filter matches (run-list.tsx:282-314). RunInspectorView separates loading, unavailable and error (run-inspector.tsx:54-63) and gives each section its own empty sentence. ToolsUsed separates failed, loading and empty (tool-uses.tsx:262-274). The workspace states an empty plan, no artifacts and no role map in words (run-workspace.tsx:531, 643, 734-736).

strengths.title: Accessible states and semantic tokens throughout
strengths.evidence: There are no color literals in scope, and every state color sits beside words: StateLine (run-list.tsx:136-143), and the header badge is aria-hidden because the status sentence says the same (run-workspace.tsx:364-371). Tool outcomes are announced through a polite live region (tool-uses.tsx:257-261), and the tool table has a caption and scoped headers (159-199). The filter buttons use aria-pressed (run-list.tsx:239), and Details sets aria-expanded and aria-controls (366-369).

strengths.title: Comments explain why and trace to decisions and stories
strengths.evidence: Examples: run-workspace.tsx:117-118 (US-15.24, SE-03), 125-126 (how live pieces join the text), 143 (Decision 0017 Q13) and 236; run-disclosure.tsx:53 (why bodies are drained), 86 (the server rule it mirrors) and 99-102; run-panel.tsx:83 (why the loaded version is sent); run-controls.tsx:17 (SP-010).

strengths.title: Key types derived from generated DTOs, and thin Server Component pages
strengths.evidence: run-panel.tsx:15 derives Task from RunWorkspace, and lines 22-26 key MARKER_TEXT by Task['marker'], so a new marker value fails the type check. The pages await Next 16's async params and set metadata (apps/web/app/runs/[id]/page.tsx:7-13). The list page wraps its useSearchParams consumer in Suspense (apps/web/app/runs/page.tsx:10-17).

findings.title: RunWorkspaceView is a 677-line, complexity-39 component that every run story edits

locations.note: RunWorkspaceView: 8 useState hooks, 3 effects and all rendering
Stream effect: snapshot load, replay loop, EventSource listeners, reconnect timer and deduplication
Derives the published result, downloads it, and runs a second snapshot fetch path
Render tree: header, 12 Section blocks, unknown outcomes, tools and parent link
Module-level status maps and pure helpers (describe, withDelta, known)
Product rule computed inline in JSX
Money arithmetic and outstanding totals computed inline in JSX

findings.evidence: ESLint, with the review's extra rules, measures RunWorkspaceView at 677 lines with complexity 39 (metrics.md section 7), the largest and most complex function in apps/web. The one function has six jobs. (1) Data loading: refresh() reads /workspace (183-196), a loop replays /events pages (243-272), a counter triggers a second refresh (316-331), and an effect downloads the newest published artifact (294-314). (2) Event stream and reconnects: an EventSource with run, live, cursor, gap and end listeners, a fixed 1 s retry and a closed flag (198-240, 274-279). (3) Deduplication: a Map keyed by sequence plus a 'sequence <= cursor' guard (175-181, 208). (4) Live text: merged through withDelta (213-220). (5) Derived view state, computed during render: the newest published artifact, the sorted timeline, the tool-event count, the summarizer rule, outstanding totals and dollar conversions (283-293, 356-357, 430-433, 576-578, 744-748, 795-826). (6) Rendering about fifteen regions. git log shows 17 commits touching the file, for 16 stories from US-4.6 to US-15.24.
findings.impact: Every run-facing story edits this one function, so diffs mix stream behavior with markup and reviewers must read both. The reconnect and deduplication state machine cannot be tested without a browser. Each live text delta (setLive, line 219) re-renders every region and sorts or filters the event map three times.
findings.recommendation: Split it in behavior-preserving steps, keeping every data-* hook and sentence that the Playwright specs read. (1) Move the pure helpers and view-model derivations to lib/runs/*.ts, with node:test coverage (WRUN-15). (2) Extract useRunWorkspace, which holds the load state machine (WRUN-02) and the ordered refresh (WRUN-04), and useRunEvents, which does replay, EventSource, backoff, deduplication and live text. (3) Extract one component per region. RunWorkspaceView should end as composition under 60 lines. Run the db profile's browser suites after each step.
findings.sketch:
lib/runs/run-events.ts        pure: describeEvent (exhaustive switch), mergeEvents, withDelta, parseCursorFrame,

The split moves only browser code, so business transitions stay on the server. Decision 0021 R1 froze data-* hooks and wording only for its own change, but the specs still read them, so they are preserved.
findings.verifierNote: Re-read every cited range: eight useState hooks, three effects and the six jobs sit where stated. eslint.json gives 677 lines and complexity 39, with the stream effect alone at 104 lines, and git log --follow lists 17 commits: 16 story deliveries and the Studio redesign.

findings.title: The run page treats every failed read as temporary: denied runs are polled every second, and 403, 422, 5xx or contract errors never leave Loading

locations.note: refresh(): on 401 or 404 it sets unavailable but still returns false; any other status just returns false; the body is never read; the parse is unguarded
start(): every false result schedules another attempt
retry(): a fixed 1 s delay, no cap and no final state
Shows 'Reconnecting. Showing the last known state.' when no state exists
Replay parse is unguarded, so a throw silently ends both the loop and the stream
Run reads can return 403 'forbidden' or 'workspace_required' ('Choose a workspace.')
A malformed run id such as /runs/abc fails the UUID path parameter and returns 422
The inspector tells a 403 or 422 to 'check that the local API is running'

findings.impact: A mistyped link, a session with several workspaces and no choice made, or contract drift between the API and the client leaves the user on an endless loading message that is also misleading, while the page sends a request every second. Drift shows up only as an unhandled rejection in the console. DH-06's denied, unavailable and retryable states are not told apart.
findings.recommendation: Give useRunWorkspace an explicit load state machine. 401 is signed_out. 403 is denied, showing the ErrorResponse message. 404 and 422 are not_found, with no retry and no stream. 5xx and network failures are retryable, with capped exponential backoff and a visible Retry button. A ContractError or invalid JSON is invalid: stop, say that the page and the API disagree, and log the ContractError path. Drain or cancel every non-ok body. Show the reconnecting sentence only when a snapshot is on screen. Add Playwright cases for 403, 422 and a malformed body using page.route, and give RunInspectorView and RunList the same classification.
findings.ruleCheck: DH-06: 'Represent loading, empty, denied, unavailable and retryable states deliberately' and 'explicit response parsing at untrusted boundaries'. nextjs.md: 'explicit error/empty/loading states'. Reads stay idempotent, and no server guard changes.
findings.verifierNote: Traced refresh(), start() and retry(): a 401 or 404 shows the unavailable text while the effect keeps requesting /workspace every second, and every other failure keeps data-state="loading" with the reconnecting sentence. The 403 and 422 shapes match settings_routes.py:52-66 and errors.py:29-32. The cross-workspace spec (run-workspace.spec.ts:267-284) asserts only the text, so nothing catches the polling.

findings.title: A lost write reply is reported as a failure, and the retry is sent with a new idempotency key

locations.note: Charge reconcile: new key on every submit; a lost reply becomes a refusal; the amount stays in the field for another submit
refusalOf(null) gives 'That could not be done. Nothing changed.'
Pause, resume and cancel: new key, same message
Panel commands: new key, same default message
Effect reconcile: new key; a null reply shows 'That couldn't be recorded.'
Buttons stay enabled while a request is in flight
The server deduplicates by an Idempotency-Key receipt and charges the oldest open call
The right pattern: the key is kept until the outcome is known, and a 5xx counts as unknown

findings.impact: An owner who follows the screen's advice can enter one provider charge twice into the run's ledger. The UI defeats the server's idempotency receipts, which exist to prevent exactly this. The defect needs a lost reply, a retry and more than one open uncertain call, but the message invites the retry.
findings.recommendation: Use ContinueRun's pattern everywhere, through one helper. Keep the key, and the exact body it was first sent with, until a definite 2xx or 4xx arrives. The server fingerprints the body with the key and refuses a reused key with different content, so RunControls must resend the version it read for the first press, and the charge field and the effect evidence stay locked meanwhile. Treat a null reply or a 5xx as unknown, and say 'This may have been recorded. Pressing again won't record it twice.' Disable every action button while a request is pending. Show refusals with role='alert' and the destructive icon, as RunControls does. Add a Playwright case that lets the request reach the API, aborts the reply (route.fetch, then route.abort), retries, and checks that exactly one charge was recorded.
findings.ruleCheck: DH-06: 'Disable duplicate submits with server idempotency as the correctness mechanism'. The change uses the server's existing receipts and expected-version guard as designed and weakens no guard. AGENTS.md's receipt requirements are not touched.
findings.verifierNote: Four fresh-key sites confirmed (run-controls.tsx:81 and 110, run-panel.tsx:91, unknown-effects.tsx:46). A second effect is possible only for the charge: pause, resume and cancel carry expected_version, and an effect must still be unknown (reconciliation.py:88-91), so there the harm is the unproven 'Nothing changed'. Revised the recommendation and sketch: the receipt fingerprints include the body (application/runs.py:408-410, run_routes.py:450), so a retry must resend the first body, including the version RunControls read for the first press.

findings.title: Write replies and stream frames are cast instead of parsed, although generated parsers exist

locations.note: The admission reply is cast; parseRunAccepted is generated (generated.ts:8534)
Error body cast
Error body cast
Error body cast
Error body cast; parseErrorResponse is generated (generated.ts:7698)
The stream's cursor frame is cast, and a NaN would persist
The event page is cast to { events?: unknown[] }, and the envelope is parsed with its events blanked

findings.impact: A contract mismatch shows up as a wrong link, a reconnect loop that never ends, or a missing timeline row, instead of a visible, logged error.
findings.recommendation: Parse the admission reply with parseRunAccepted. Add readErrorResponse(reply): Promise<ErrorResponse | null>, which wraps parseErrorResponse in try/catch. Add a pure parseCursorFrame(data): number | null that accepts only safe non-negative integers, and a pure splitEventPage(raw: unknown) that requires an events array and returns the known events plus a count of skipped ones. In known(), skip only payload types outside the generated union, and log a known type that fails validation with its ContractError path.
findings.ruleCheck: DH-06: 'No blanket type assertions to conceal contract mismatches' and 'explicit response parsing at untrusted boundaries'. contracts.md: TypeScript types do not validate JSON. Decision 0017 Q13 still holds, because unknown event types are still ignored. Generated files are consumed, not edited.
findings.verifierNote: Raised from medium to high: the rubric rates hidden contract drift at a trust boundary high, the stream's frames have no schema the drift check could compare (event_routes.py:226), and WCMP-02 rates the same admission-reply cast high. All casts and the NaN path were confirmed; the evidence now says which of the ten assertions can hide drift.

findings.title: Every stored event refetches the whole snapshot, and an older reply can overwrite a newer one

locations.note: Each run frame adds the event and starts a full /workspace fetch
Each gap frame does the same
Replies are applied in the order they arrive, without a check
A second refresh path, driven by a counter and not coordinated with the first
RunWorkspace.cursor exists but is never read
cursor is the run's event_sequence at read time (the column is selected at line 84)
The tool-event count is ToolsUsed's reload trigger
Each change of that count reloads every tool-use page from after=0

findings.evidence: Stored events come in bursts (tool.use.started, tool.use.completed, run.status_changed) as consecutive run frames. Each frame starts its own GET, and each reply calls setSnapshot unconditionally. The DTO's cursor, which the projection fills from runs.event_sequence, could order the replies, but the client never reads it. read_workspace makes at least 14 database calls per refresh. ToolsUsed reloads every page whenever the tool-event count changes, and setLive re-renders the whole workspace for each live delta.
findings.impact: If an earlier reply resolves last, the page shows older state. After a run's final events nothing comes later to correct it, so the header and controls can show a non-terminal status after the timeline says 'Run moved from verifying to succeeded'. Long runs also make reads proportional to their event count.
findings.recommendation: In useRunWorkspace, allow one request in flight and at most one queued refresh. Apply a reply only when its snapshot.cursor is at least the shown cursor; an equal cursor is harmless. Send the after-action refresh through the same function. Have ToolsUsed refetch only from its first unfinished use and merge the rows by id, since the list pages by id and a started use changes when it completes; when every loaded use is finished, fetch after the last id. Let ResultSection own the live text so a delta re-renders one region, and memoize the values derived from events.
findings.ruleCheck: DH-06: 'Browser state is a view of durable state'. Ordering snapshots by the server's event_sequence keeps it a faithful view. The reconnect and deduplication behavior required by nextjs.md is unchanged.
findings.verifierNote: refresh() applies every reply unconditionally (194); RunWorkspace.cursor (generated.ts:8729) comes from runs.event_sequence (run_projection.py:84 and 373), and nothing in apps/web reads it. Revised one step: the tool-use list pages by id (tool_uses.py:277-278), so fetching only after the last loaded id, as first proposed, would miss a started use that later completes. The race is reasoned from the code, not reproduced.

findings.title: Contract unions are widened to string, so a new status or outcome passes the type check and renders blank

locations.note: STATUS_TEXT, STATUS_LABEL and STATUS_TONE are keyed by string
ROLE_SOURCE is keyed by string; BindingSource is generated (generated.ts:7533)
STATUS_TEXT and tone(status: string); StateLine also takes a string (127)
PROFILE_NAMES is keyed by string; ModelProfileId is generated (generated.ts:8144)
TERMINAL and PAUSABLE are Set<string>; commandsFor takes status: string, as does the prop at line 53
OUTCOMES and OutcomeIcon take string
A hand-written Operation type duplicates the generated UnknownEffect; outcome is a string at line 37
describe(): an if-chain whose last branch labels any unmatched payload with a name field 'Artifact ... is missing'; tsc already rejects a new type without one

findings.evidence: Seven lookup maps, the TERMINAL and PAUSABLE sets and six parameters use string where a generated union exists (RunStatus is at generated.ts:8691). There is also one hand-written DTO type and one non-exhaustive dispatch. With noUncheckedIndexedAccess, each lookup returns string | undefined. A status added to the Python enum therefore type-checks, then renders an empty status sentence (392) and no header badge (363), and commandsFor offers Cancel because the new status is in neither TERMINAL nor PAUSABLE. run-panel.tsx:22 already shows the safer form, Record<Task['marker'], string>. A related cause belongs to another area: the generator maps ExpertBinding.role_bindings, declared in Pydantic as dict[str, str], to Record<string, unknown> (scripts/generate_contracts.py:46-47). That is why run-disclosure.tsx:34 and 78 and run-workspace.tsx:723-727 handle unknown values.
findings.impact: After the client is regenerated, tsc still passes while the UI silently mishandles the new value, so reviewers must find every map by hand.
findings.recommendation: Key the maps by the generated unions: Record<RunStatus, string>, Record<BindingSource, string>, Record<NonNullable<ToolUseView['outcome']>, string> and Record<ModelProfileId, string>. Type the parameters with the same unions. Use UnknownEffect and EffectEvidence['outcome'] in UnknownEffects. Turn describe() into a switch on payload.type that ends in assertNever(payload). Keep a runtime fallback for values the client doesn't know, as Decision 0017 Q13 requires. Report the role_bindings mapping to the contracts owner.
findings.ruleCheck: DH-06: use generated API types. contracts.md: generated TypeScript consumes the API definitions. The UI view maps stay separate from the DTOs and are only keyed by DTO unions, so no types are merged.
findings.verifierNote: Recounted: seven maps, the TERMINAL and PAUSABLE sets, six parameters, the hand-written Operation type and describe() make 17, not 15. describe() is narrower than first stated: tsc already rejects a new payload type without a name field at line 114, and parseRunEvent drops unknown types at runtime, so only a new type with a name field would be mislabeled.

findings.evidence: There is one import cycle and six imports between screens. All 43 component files sit flat in apps/web/components. Shared run vocabulary (STATUS_TEXT, StateLine), the command rule (commandsFor), a data hook (useToolUses), a budget default and a DOM id all live inside screen modules, so other screens depend on whole screens.
findings.impact: Dependencies run sideways between screens. The cycle makes module evaluation order matter if either file gains top-level effects. The pieces extracted in WRUN-01 and WRUN-05 have no home. The 'goal' id contract breaks silently if the composer renames its input.
findings.recommendation: Add lib/runs/ for pure logic and components/runs/ for shared run widgets. Screens import from those folders, never from each other. Move DEFAULT_BUDGET_MICRO_USD to lib/runs/budget.ts. Export a GOAL_INPUT_ID constant that both the composer input and focusGoal use. Move wallTime, with a test, to lib/runs/format.ts.
